title.narrative: Projet de réponse d’urgence de Gestion des VBG et d’assistance aux populations affectées par des chocs récents de Nana-Bakassa et Nangha-Boguila en Secal.

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtThis Action proposes to pursue 2 sectoral objectives, namely GBV and SECAL:lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltfontgtThis project will take into account the AAP guideline annexed to the strategic document of the first standard allocation 2024. Therefore, accountability will be at the center, including the broad involvement of all communities in the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Beneficiaries will be included in the design of activities at different stages of the project. Firstly, the mapping of protection risks will be established following the establishment of focus groups composed of women, men, girls and boys, and will be the starting point for the implementation of the project. Then, the choice of socio-economic activities will be made in collaboration with women's groups to ensure that the needs expressed are in line with the humanitarian response provided by AFEB. ltbrgtIn GBV, objective 1 consists of: Monitoring and case management of survivors of Gender-Based Violence/PSEA with the distribution of dignity kits. ltbrgt1. Establish safe and secure spaces for women and girls with related services. ltbrgt2. Establish mobile GBV protection teams in collaboration with other humanitarian sectors such as the health cluster to make available a minimum GBV package for survivors in hard-to-reach areas. ltbrgtWhile Objective 2 aims to: Prevent and mitigate the risks associated with GBV and PSEA by organizing awareness raising among men, women, boys and girls and available services, training adolescent girls on GBV and life skills as an innovation in CAR, where a wide range of psychosocial and interpersonal skills that help people make informed decisions will be put in place, communicate more effectively and develop coping and self-management skills that can help them lead healthier and more productive lives. ltbrgt3. Strengthen the socio-economic capacity of women and girls, including survivors of GBV, through group activities (socio-economic reintegration of survivors). ltbrgt4. Organize activities to involve men and community leaders in the fight against violence against women and girls and the training of health providers on the care of survivors of GBV, as an innovation, interventions guided by women's voices to engage men and boys to be true allies of women and girls in the context of CAR, positive masculinity. ltbrgt5. Organize training for health providers in the areas targeted by the projects on the clinical management of rape and intimate partner violence in collaboration with the health cluster and the Health Districts. ltbrgtIn Secal, the objective of this action is to ensure that the dignity of people in situations of acute food insecurity (IPC phases 4 and 3) in Nana-Bakassa and Nangha-Boguila is preserved through emergency food assistance. It is therefore a question of providing additional emergency food assistance in the form of food and Cash to cover 80% of the needs of new IDPs, returnees, spontaneous repatriates for 3 months, and providing direct food assistance in the form of food and Cash to cover 60% of the needs of host, returnee, spontaneous returnees and long-term IDPs for a period of 6 months and Cash food assistance to households and also to restore and strengthen the livelihoods of the acutely food insecure populations through the provision of emergency assistance by the food, vegetable and small ruminant growing seasons in order to prevent negative coping mechanisms and thus support the recovery and recovery of the population. resilience. This project will help avoid the risk of GBV associated to daily struggle in women's and girls' life. lt/fontgtlt/pgt
